A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PIPA work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B are readable and can be matched despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original GSM8K and MATH experiments using Deepseek and Qwen models in Table 1, alongside ablations and training analyses in Section 3.3.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark results, ablations, and training analyses in Table 1 and Section 3.3.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same PIPA-M/PIPA-N objectives, prior constraints, shared transformer and value head, and token-level treatment. The rewritten parameterization explains the existing procedure; the numerical clipping-setting revision is covered under E3 and D1.

E1.justification: Both versions use the AlphaMath data containing GSM8K/MATH problems and CoT/TIR solutions, with the same paired/unpaired and answer-level/step-level scenarios. General-task evaluation remains future work rather than added coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same DPO, IPO, KTO, Step-DPO, and Step-KTO comparators in their corresponding settings. Appendix B retains the same baseline adaptations, and the additional-SFT comparisons in Table 4 are unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 2.6 changes the reported PIPA-M clipping epsilon from 10^-10 to 10^-6. Dataset construction, annotation threshold, models, training schedules, learning-rate search, and decoding settings otherwise match. This establishes a reported setting revision, not that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 3.3 retains the value-head ablation, alternative priors, additional SFT loss, value-model trajectories, DPO reward curves, and annotation-threshold analysis. Their evidence is unchanged; relocated plots do not constitute additional analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The reporting practice remains single benchmark scores and training curves.

E6.justification: All numerical results in Tables 1–4 and the plotted results in Figures 3–5 are retained. Section 2.2 newly reports the qualitative observation that the PIPA-M parameterization rarely produces probabilities exceeding one in practice, without providing a frequency or supporting measurements.

T1.justification: Equation 1 changes from a generic data-loss formulation to conditional label log-likelihood. The rewrite removes v1's instruction to minimize log-likelihood, but v2 Equation 3 inconsistently omits the logarithm. Theorem 2.1's parameterization is otherwise restated equivalently through Bayes' rule, and Appendix A retains the substantive DPO/KTO equivalences and proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims: a probabilistic preference-alignment framework, DPO/KTO connections, support for unpaired and step-level data, and reported 3–10% improvements without additional computational overhead.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 newly explains the choice of mathematical reasoning as the testbed and explicitly leaves systematic general-task evaluation to future work. Existing interpretations concerning prior choice, distribution shift, value learning, and the usefulness of step-level annotations are retained.

D1.justification: v2 revises the clipping epsilon, newly identifies Deepseek in the Figure 3 discussion, and acknowledges computing support from the Vista GPU Cluster. The added 'step-wise' description of Figure 3 conflicts with its retained answer-level and step-level curves, so it does not establish a changed experiment.

R1.justification: v2 adds Liu et al. (2024d), 'Provably mitigating overoptimization in RLHF,' to the reward-curve discussion and references. It also explicitly discusses Dumoulin et al.'s density-estimation recovery of DPO in related work; that work was already cited in v1. The broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites in Sections 2.1–2.4 expand the parameterization explanation and explain decoupling preference pairs. v2 also adds acknowledgments and an impact statement. Most prose and the main section and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: The document is extensively restyled into ICML/PMLR format, changing typography, title and affiliation layout, running headers, captions, and reference presentation. Figures and tables are resized and repositioned, including a much smaller text-wrapped Figure 5. The five underlying figure graphics and table contents are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 provides clearer parameterization explanations, an explicit boundary on empirical coverage, and useful implementation and literature context. However, it removes v1's erroneous log-likelihood minimization wording while introducing an unlogged objective in Equation 3, and its new Figure 3 setting description conflicts with the retained plot. With the experimental evidence unchanged, these modest documentation benefits and mathematical/reporting inconsistencies prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
